newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ Nov futures end up, rangebound before report.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ Nov futures end up, rangebound before report.

text.p: NYCE November frozen concentrated orange juice futures closed higher in thin dealings as players dismissed an encroaching tropical storm in the Gulf of Mexico.

Tropical Storm Josephine is forecast to hit Florida Tuesday, but is not expected to wreak damage on the state's citrus groves. Mike Palmerino, a meteorologist with Weather Services Corp said the storm will most likely hit north of the citrus-growing region, bringing beneficial rains.
Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis said the storm could cause fruit droppage and tree damage in the northern portion of the citrus belt.

Players, meanwhile, await Friday's U.S. Department of Agriculture estimate for the 1996/97 Florida crop. Industry sources expect the USDA to rais its estimate from the previous forecast for 203.2 million 90-lb boxes, to between 215 million and 225 million boxes.
Prices will likely drift rangebound ahead of the report. Support remained at 103.00 and resistance between 115.00 and 116.00, basis the November contract.
November closed up 1.40 at 114.60, having ranged from 114.90 to 112.50. The back months ended 0.20 lower to up 0.35. Volume was estimated at 1,300 lots.
Dealers cited short-covering in the November/January spread, light speculative and fund buying in the spot month and trade scale up selling.
